Section 1: The Premise of the Company

Copart, Inc. (NASDAQ: CPRT) represents a quintessential, high-return-on-invested-capital (ROIC) natural duopoly in global vehicle remarketing and salvage auction services. Operating across a network of over 250 physical storage facilities spanning 11 countries, Copart serves as the indispensable central clearinghouse connecting insurance carriers, commercial fleets, rental companies, and financial institutions (consignors) with a global buyer base of over 1 million registered members in more than 185 countries—comprising licensed dismantlers, rebuilders, used vehicle dealers, and cross-border exporters. Through its Virtual Bidding Third Generation (VB3) proprietary auction platform, Copart processes over 4 million vehicles annually, extracting two distinct streams of value: high-margin, low-capital-intensity transaction fees from service revenues (approx. 87% of total revenues) and direct principal resale revenue from purchased vehicle inventory (approx. 13% of total revenues).

The economic engine of Copart rests on two powerful structural tailwinds: the secular upward trajectory of US Total Loss Frequency (TLF) and the self-reinforcing network effect of cross-border bidding liquidity. Total Loss Frequency—the percentage of vehicle collision claims deemed economically unrepairable by insurance carriers—has expanded from approximately 15% a decade ago to over 21% today. This shift is driven by the structural inflation of vehicle repair costs, including the ubiquitous integration of modern Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), complex electronic sensor suites, structural aluminum, and elevated body shop labor rates. When collision repair costs approach 60%–70% of a vehicle's Pre-Accident Value (PAV), insurance carriers rationalize total loss settlements and consign the salvage vehicle to Copart. Furthermore, Copart's deliberate 30-year strategy of acquiring and owning real estate outright (owning >85% of its 10,000+ acre footprint rather than leasing) creates an unassailable physical moat. Salvage storage yards face severe localized municipal zoning, environmental licensing, and NIMBY ("Not In My Backyard") regulatory barriers. This physical asset network, combined with global buyer liquidity that maximizes recovery yields for insurers, forms a structural tollbridge that competitors cannot replicate.

A rigorous examination of Copart's audited statutory filings (Form 10-K for FY2025 ended July 31, 2025, and Form 10-Q filings through Q3 FY2026 ended April 30, 2026) and 4-quarter management commentary highlights exceptional operational consistency, even amidst post-pandemic used vehicle price normalization. Under the leadership of returned Chief Executive Officer Jay Adair and President Jane Pocock, management has prioritized disciplined organic capacity expansion, international infrastructure buildout across the UK, Germany, Spain, and the Middle East, and aggressive capital return via share repurchases ($1.1B to $1.6B allocated across FY2025–FY2026). While Average Selling Prices (ASPs) per vehicle have moderated from peak supply-chain dislocation levels, unit volume growth and expanding international buyer participation have sustained operating margins near 36.5%–37.0%.

Economic Moat & Business Predictability Audits

1. Pricing Power Audit: Copart exhibits exceptional pricing power rooted in market dynamics rather than arbitrary fee increases. Insurance carriers assign total loss vehicles to Copart because Copart's global buyer liquidity delivers higher recovery values (higher net proceeds at auction) than competing channels. A $100 increase in buyer fee tiers is overwhelmingly offset by higher auction sale proceeds. Copart systematically adjusts its tiered buyer fee schedule periodically without unit volume attrition. Consignor seller fees remain contractual, protected by high switching costs—renegotiating yard logistics, title transfer integration, and carrier pickup dispatch across hundreds of regional yards requires immense operational friction for insurance carriers.

2. Structural Moat Audit: Copart's moat is double-barreled: physical real estate control and two-sided digital network effects. Owning over 10,000 acres of land across 250+ locations creates a structural barrier to entry. Obtaining municipal permits and zoning approvals for salvage vehicle storage in major metropolitan areas is virtually impossible for new entrants today. On the demand side, connecting over 1 million registered buyers across 185 countries creates a bidding density where every additional buyer increases the recovery value for insurance sellers, which in turn attracts more insurance vehicle assignments. This duopoly structure alongside IAA (RB Global) ensures high competitive durability.

3. Business Predictability Audit: Copart ranks among the most operational predictable businesses in specialty services. Vehicle accident frequency is anchored to total vehicle miles driven, adverse weather events, and driver distraction trends. Total loss frequency is structurally rising due to vehicle electronics complexity. While used vehicle ASP fluctuations introduce minor quarter-to-quarter variability in fee realization, unit volumes remain uncorrelated with broader economic recessions—in downturns, consumers retain older vehicles longer, increasing average fleet age and total loss probability upon collision.

Section 2: The Probable Future Paths

Based on the company's audited statutory filings, segment dynamics, and 4-quarter management commentary, here are the distinct, un-biased operational paths covering 90%–95% of the fundamental probability space over the next 3–5 years:

Path 1: Core Execution & Structural Total Loss Compounder (70% Probability Weight)

Copart delivers steady execution of its core strategy, benefiting from rising US total loss frequency, expanding international buyer liquidity, and disciplined yard capacity expansion while preserving operating margins above 36.5%.

Under this path, total loss frequency continues its secular advance from ~21.0% toward ~22.5% across major US auto insurers, driven by complex ADAS sensor replacement costs and elevated repair shop labor rates. Copart's global buyer base expands at 4%–5% annually, deepening cross-border bidding liquidity and supporting firm vehicle ASP recoveries. Management continues to deploy capital efficiently, purchasing 300–500 additional acres annually to expand yard intake capacity near congested metro areas, while executing opportunistic share buybacks using surplus cash flow.

Operational Unit Drivers & Revenue:

  • Processed Unit Volume: Global processed auction units grow at a 5.5% CAGR, rising from 4.25 million units in FY2025 to 5.00 million units in FY2028.
  • Service Pricing / ARPU: Blended service fee realization per unit (consignor + buyer fees) increases from $960 per unit in FY2025 to $1,034 per unit in FY2028 (2.5% annual growth), supported by tiered fee schedule adjustments and expanded title procurement services.
  • Service Revenue Derivation: 5.00 million units × $1,034 per unit = $5,170.0 million USD in FY2028.
  • Vehicle Sales Revenue: Principal resales stabilize at $630.0 million USD in FY2028.
  • Total Consolidated Revenue: $5,170.0M + $630.0M = $5,800.0 million USD in FY2028 (7.6% CAGR over FY2025 baseline).

Cost Structure, CapEx & Owner Earnings:

  • Operating Margin: Expands modestly to 37.0% due to fixed cost absorption across owned yard infrastructure, yielding GAAP Operating Income of $2,146.0 million USD in FY2028.
  • GAAP Operating Cash Flow (OCF): $2,100.0 million USD.
  • Reinvestment & CapEx: Maintenance CapEx scales to $210.0 million USD (3.6% of revenue); Growth CapEx for land acquisition is $320.0 million USD. SBC remains controlled at $80.0 million USD (~3.8% of OCF).
  • Normalized Owner Earnings (OE₂₀₂₈): $2,100.0M OCF - $210.0M Maintenance CapEx - $80.0M SBC = $1,810.0 million USD.
  • Per Share Owner Earnings: Assuming $1.2B in share buybacks reduces diluted share count from 965.2M to 940.0M shares, FY2028 OE per share reaches $1.93 USD ($1,810.0M / 940.0M shares), representing a 9.3% per-share OE CAGR.

Adversarial Red-Team Stress-Test: The central risk to Path 1 is a rapid deflation in used vehicle values, which would reduce variable buyer transaction fees, or a temporary decrease in total loss assignments if insurers adjust total loss threshold formulas downward. Falsification Metric: A decline in global processed unit growth below 2.0% YoY for two consecutive quarters, or a drop in blended service revenue per unit below $920 USD, falsifies this compounding trajectory.

Quarterly Milestones: Track US Total Loss Frequency metrics in quarterly disclosures (maintaining >21.0%); verify international buyer volume growth (>5% YoY); monitor quarterly land acquisition announcements (>75 acres added per quarter).

Path 2: Execution Friction & Cyclical ASP Margin Drag (20% Probability Weight)

Copart encounters operational headwinds from softening used car ASPs, inflationary towing and labor expenses, and temporary slowing in total loss assignment growth, compressing operating margins by ~220 bps.

In this trajectory, post-pandemic normalization of used car prices accelerates, causing average auction vehicle prices to fall 8%–10%. Because buyer fee schedules are tiered relative to vehicle ASPs, lower sale prices directly reduce fee realization per vehicle. Simultaneously, third-party towing subcontractor rates and yard labor wage inflation elevate facility operational costs. Insurance carriers, responding to lower vehicle values, temporarily tighten total loss thresholds, slowing unit volume growth in the US market.

Operational Unit Drivers & Revenue:

  • Processed Unit Volume: Global processed auction units grow at a sluggish 2.5% CAGR, reaching 4.58 million units in FY2028.
  • Service Pricing / ARPU: Blended service fee realization per unit contracts to $950 per unit in FY2028 due to lower vehicle ASPs depressing variable buyer transaction fees.
  • Service Revenue Derivation: 4.58 million units × $950 per unit = $4,351.0 million USD in FY2028.
  • Vehicle Sales Revenue: Softens to $570.0 million USD due to lower used car pricing on principal inventory.
  • Total Consolidated Revenue: $4,351.0M + $570.0M = $4,921.0 million USD in FY2028 (1.9% CAGR over FY2025 baseline).

Cost Structure, CapEx & Owner Earnings:

  • Operating Margin: Compresses 220 bps from FY2025 baseline to 34.3%, driven by higher diesel/towing expenses and fixed yard maintenance costs, generating Operating Income of $1,688.0 million USD in FY2028.
  • GAAP Operating Cash Flow (OCF): Softens to $1,620.0 million USD.
  • Reinvestment & CapEx: Maintenance CapEx elevates to $200.0 million USD due to equipment replacement cost inflation; Growth CapEx slows to $220.0 million USD. SBC rises to $75.0 million USD.
  • Normalized Owner Earnings (OE₂₀₂₈): $1,620.0M OCF - $200.0M Maintenance CapEx - $75.0M SBC = $1,345.0 million USD.
  • Per Share Owner Earnings: With slower buybacks reducing share count to 955.0M shares, FY2028 OE per share declines slightly to $1.41 USD ($1,345.0M / 955.0M shares).

Adversarial Red-Team Stress-Test: The key operational failure point is persistent cost inflation in towing logistics without the ability to pass costs to consignors. Falsification Metric: GAAP Operating Margin falling below 33.5% for two consecutive quarters, or facility operating expenses exceeding 44.0% of service revenues, confirms Path 2 execution friction.

Quarterly Milestones: Monitor facility operating costs as a percentage of service revenue (threshold >42.5%); track unit fee realization drops (>3% YoY contraction); watch for insurance carrier loss ratio commentary indicating reduced total loss processing.

Path 3: Operating Leverage & Tech-Driven Outperformance (10% Probability Weight)

Accelerating vehicle complexity pushes total loss frequency above 23.5%, while automated AI titling and international market share gains drive operating margins to 38.6% and double-digit OE growth.

Under this optimistic execution path, electric vehicle (EV) penetration and autonomous driving features (lidar, radar, recalibration costs) cause collision repair costs to surge, forcing insurance carriers to declare total losses on milder accidents. US total loss frequency breaks above 23.5%. Internationally, Copart wins major exclusive insurance supply contracts in Germany and Spain, dislodging legacy fragmented dismantler networks. Internally, Copart deploys AI-automated title processing and proprietary computer-vision vehicle imaging, reducing manual yard labor and administrative turnaround times by 20%.

Operational Unit Drivers & Revenue:

  • Processed Unit Volume: Global processed auction units surge at an 8.5% CAGR, reaching 5.43 million units in FY2028.
  • Service Pricing / ARPU: Blended service fee realization per unit reaches $1,080 per unit in FY2028, supported by strong cross-border bidding liquidity driving higher vehicle ASPs and premium condition-report fees.
  • Service Revenue Derivation: 5.43 million units × $1,080 per unit = $5,864.4 million USD in FY2028.
  • Vehicle Sales Revenue: Expands to $700.0 million USD.
  • Total Consolidated Revenue: $5,864.4M + $700.0M = $6,564.4 million USD in FY2028 (12.2% CAGR over FY2025 baseline).

Cost Structure, CapEx & Owner Earnings:

  • Operating Margin: Expands 210 bps to 38.6% as digital title automation lowers G&A overhead and high auction volume maximizes owned land operational leverage. Operating Income hits $2,533.8 million USD in FY2028.
  • GAAP Operating Cash Flow (OCF): Reaches $2,500.0 million USD.
  • Reinvestment & CapEx: Maintenance CapEx scales to $220.0 million USD; Growth CapEx ramps to $400.0 million USD to capture international share. SBC equals $85.0 million USD.
  • Normalized Owner Earnings (OE₂₀₂₈): $2,500.0M OCF - $220.0M Maintenance CapEx - $85.0M SBC = $2,195.0 million USD.
  • Per Share Owner Earnings: Aggressive share repurchases reduce diluted share count to 930.0M shares, pushing FY2028 OE per share to $2.36 USD ($2,195.0M / 930.0M shares), representing a 16.8% per-share OE CAGR.

Adversarial Red-Team Stress-Test: The risk to Path 3 is over-capitalization in international markets where insurance consignment norms differ from the US, leading to lower-than-projected asset turnover. Falsification Metric: International segment revenue growth slowing below 8% YoY or failure to achieve international gross margins above 38.0% falsifies Path 3 outperformance.

Quarterly Milestones: Track US Total Loss Frequency reaching >22.5%; observe international revenue growth accelerating above >12.0% YoY; confirm GAAP Operating Margins exceeding 38.0% in quarterly 10-Q filings.

Section 3: Normalized Owner Earnings Multiple & Yield Inversion Valuation

To establish a rigorous, fundamental appraisal of Copart, Inc. (CPRT), we deploy a multi-year Owner Earnings compounding model anchored strictly in Benjamin Graham and Warren Buffett valuation principles. We reject academic Capital Asset Pricing Models (CAPM) and arbitrary beta assumptions, adopting instead a level-headed equity opportunity cost hurdle rate of 9.5%. Baseline Owner Earnings (OE₀) for FY2025 stand at $1,431.3 million USD, or $1.48 per diluted share (derived from $1,680.4M GAAP Operating Cash Flow less $180.0M Maintenance CapEx and $69.1M stock-based compensation cash expense). Furthermore, Copart's balance sheet represents an unassailable fortress, holding $3,967.2 million USD in net surplus liquid cash ($4.11 per diluted share after deducting an operational working capital buffer and all funded debt/lease liabilities).

In evaluating terminal capitalization multiples at Year 5, we apply the strictly mathematically grounded Gordon Growth / ROIC framework: Terminal Multiple = (1 - g / ROIC) / (r - g), where r = 9.5%. Because Copart operates as an asset-light tollbridge with returns on invested capital exceeding 25%–30%, capital required to support incremental growth is minimal. For Path 1, a 9.3% per-share OE compounding rate maps to a 20.0x terminal multiple (a 5.0% Owner Cash Yield). For Path 2, execution friction and cyclical margin drag reduce 5-year growth to 1.5% per annum, compressing the terminal multiple to 14.0x (a 7.1% Owner Cash Yield). For Path 3, accelerated international expansion and AI automation propel OE growth to 15.0% per annum, justifying a 23.0x terminal multiple (a 4.3% Owner Cash Yield).

Empirical Probability Weighting Rationale

Path 1 (70% Weight): Assigned dominant weight based on 10-K statutory disclosures confirming steady gains in US Total Loss Frequency (>21.0%), persistent expansion of international buyer registration (+5% YoY), and Copart's multi-decade track record of disciplined organic land accumulation. This represents the primary, highly predictable operating trajectory of the enterprise.

Path 2 (20% Weight): Assigned realistic downside risk weight to capture cyclical normalization in used vehicle ASPs from peak supply-chain dislocation levels, alongside inflationary pressures on third-party towing sub-contractors and municipal yard labor expenses noted in recent 10-Q management discussion.

Path 3 (10% Weight): Assigned conservative upside weight reflecting potential structural acceleration in total loss frequency above 23.5% driven by rapid EV/ADAS electronic repair inflation, coupled with scalable digital title automation and international market share capture in Europe.

Market Inversion & Valuation Synthesis

Implied Market Reality: At today's market price of $34.33, after deducting $4.11 per share in unencumbered net surplus cash, the market is pricing Copart's core business engine at 20.4x Normalized OE₀ (an implied operating cash yield of 4.9%). Mr. Market is currently embedding approximately 10.5%–11.5% annual OE compounding over the next 5 years.

Probability-Weighted 5-Year Target Price: $47.76 / share (Expected 5-Year Price CAGR: +6.8% / yr; Total Return: +39.1%).

Probability-Weighted Present Fair Value (9.5% Hurdle): $30.34 / share (Margin of Safety: -11.6% vs. today's market price of $34.33).

Capital Allocation Recommendation: Copart is an extraordinary, wide-moat, high-ROIC compounding enterprise protected by an unassailable physical real estate footprint and network effects. However, at $34.33 per share, the stock trades at a mild premium (~11.6%) above its probability-weighted present intrinsic fair value of $30.34. Conservative fundamental investors demanding a minimum 20% Ben Graham Margin of Safety should maintain a strict HOLD / WATCHLIST stance, awaiting a market pullback toward $24.00–$25.00 before allocating fresh capital.
